rationale: The subtracted term MAX(NEG(re),0)/lt is exactly zero for the majority of firms with positive retained earnings, so the conditioner collapses to che/act and the signal is largely a cosmetic re-run of the archived "Cash-Quality EBITDA Value" (fmb 5.11, ls_talpha 5.18), with the added defect of netting a bounded 0–1 ratio against an unbounded one.

This is a one-variable swap (pi → re) on the archived "Loss-Runway OCF Yield" and simultaneously the OCF twin of the archived "Retained-Deficit Runway EBITDA Value," i.e., a mechanical crossing of two already-tested signals rather than a new mechanism.

The weakest-link MIN over sales cheapness, EBITDA margin, and cash coverage is a genuinely different aggregation and margin is a new conditioner in this archive, though the reviewer should note that requiring high revt/P *and* high ebitda/revt largely reconstructs the already-strong EBITDA-yield-plus-liquidity family, so incremental information may be small.

Same defect as its sibling: the retained-deficit penalty is zero for most firms, so the conditioner reduces to che/lct and the signal is effectively the archived "Cash-Covered Sales Value" with a sparse perturbation, and its weakness there was portfolio alpha (0.017), which this adjustment does not plausibly address.

Because RANK(NEG(pi)/che) is taken over the full cross-section, essentially all loss firms land near the top of that rank and the multiplier is nearly constant (~0.9) within the loss subset, so the stated "loss magnitude relative to cash" intensity does almost nothing and the signal degenerates to a profitability sign flip on EBITDA yield — close to the archived "Taxpaying Deep Value" idea.

Third instance of the identical net-deficit template, and its base case is the archived "Cash-Quality Distress-Price Value," which already delivered an economically negligible alpha (0.003, t=0.30) despite a strong FMB t-stat, so a conditioner that is zero for most firms cannot credibly fix the portfolio-side failure.
